[Date]

Cigna Appeals Unit  
Please mail this appeal to the Cigna appeals address shown on the member ID card.

Re: Quinn Grant  
Member ID: W914144325  
Plan: Cigna Commercial/ACA, Illinois  
Reference number: POC-A7C9BA9551-23896  
Requested service: Total ankle replacement  
CPT: 27702  
Denial notice date: August 22, 2026

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request reversal of the denial and authorization for the requested procedure.

The publicly available Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285, Total Ankle Arthroplasty/Replacement, effective March 15, 2026, lists CPT 27702 as total ankle arthroplasty with implant. The policy states:

“Total ankle arthroplasty/replacement with a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved/cleared device* is considered medically necessary as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis when ALL of the following criteria have been met:”

“• individual is skeletally mature”

“• presence of ONE of the following in the affected ankle:  
   severe inflammatory arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis)  
   severe osteoarthritis  
   post-traumatic arthritis”

“• individual has moderate to severe ankle pain that:  
   is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration  
   interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment”

“• failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy)”

“• individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty:  
   active infection  
   insufficient bone/osteonecrosis  
   loss of musculature in the affected limb/insufficient ligament support  
   vascular insufficiency in the affected limb  
   Charcot’s or other peripheral neuropathy  
   neurological impairment  
   severe ankle deformity precluding proper alignment  
   malalignment or severe deformity of involved or adjacent anatomic structures (e.g. hindfoot, forefoot, knee)  
   absence of medial or lateral malleolus, or both  
   poor skin conditions secondary to surgical scars or trauma”

The clinical records address the criteria as follows:

1. The patient has had 14 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. Examination documents a painful, limited range of motion and positive provocative testing on the affected side.

2. The patient is limited to walking approximately two blocks and has an antalgic gait. This meets the policy’s stated example of function-limiting pain at short distances. The records also document that the pain is functionally limiting; additional documentation regarding interference with activities of daily living and/or employment is enclosed or will be provided by [patient/provider].

3. The July 7, 2026 weight-bearing ankle radiographs show tibiotalar joint-space obliteration with subchondral cysts. These findings support advanced degenerative ankle disease. The treating orthopedic surgeon’s diagnosis is [insert the documented diagnosis, such as severe ankle osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis].

4. Conservative treatment has failed. The patient used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief, received a corticosteroid injection on May 18, 2026, with only four weeks of partial relief, and completed 18 supervised physical-therapy visits from April 9 through July 2, 2026. The therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance and was documented in the physical-therapy discharge note.

5. The clinical summary documents no active infection. It also documents that the patient is a nonsmoker, has a BMI of 29, and has no untreated substance use. The treating surgeon’s confirmation regarding the remaining listed contraindications is [enclosed/provided in the attached surgical evaluation]. Specifically, please consider the surgeon’s documentation regarding bone stock, musculature and ligament support, vascular status, neuropathy or neurological impairment, deformity and alignment, malleoli, and skin condition.

6. The proposed implant is [insert the FDA-approved or FDA-cleared device name]. The patient is [insert confirmation that the patient is skeletally mature].

On the available records, the patient has prolonged moderate-to-severe, function-limiting ankle pain; radiographic evidence of advanced ankle joint destruction; failure of at least six months of medication and other conservative treatment; and no documented active infection. The patient’s walking limitation and persistent pain support the medical necessity of replacing the diseased ankle joint rather than continuing ineffective conservative care.

Please overturn the denial and approve CPT 27702. If Cigna maintains the denial, please provide a written explanation identifying each specific criterion considered unmet, the clinical records relied upon, and any clinical-review or delegated-vendor criteria used in addition to Medical Coverage Policy 0285.

Please treat this as a timely appeal of the August 22, 2026 adverse benefit determination. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received no later than February 18, 2027.

Sincerely,

Quinn Grant  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Attachments:

- August 22, 2026 denial notice  
- July 7, 2026 weight-bearing ankle radiographs and report  
- Physical-therapy discharge note  
- Medication and injection treatment records  
- Orthopedic examination and surgical evaluation  
- [Documentation of activities-of-daily-living or employment limitations]

- [Documentation identifying the FDA-approved or FDA-cleared implant]
